claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating has a nanocrystalline microstructure.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating is produced under ambient processing conditions.
At 600–900°C, the FeNiCrCoCu coating develops a continuous, adherent oxide glaze.
The high-temperature oxide glaze is rich in Cu and Cr.
The oxide glaze acts as a solid lubricant.
The oxide glaze serves as a physical barrier to direct metal-to-metal contact.
Mitigation of direct metal-to-metal contact reduces friction and wear under load.
Formation of the oxide glaze governs the coating's overall high-temperature wear resistance.
Controlled pre-oxidation will produce a more uniform and protective oxide layer than oxidation occurring in situ during wear.
The as-deposited baseline coating oxidizes spontaneously during high-temperature wear.
Elevated temperature promotes controlled oxidation of the FeNiCrCoCu surface.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower friction coefficient than as-deposited coatings during otherwise identical high-temperature wear tests.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings during otherwise identical high-temperature wear tests.
Improved friction and wear performance will correlate with detection of a uniform, robust, adherent oxide layer.
The proposed mechanism is applicable in oxidizing environments between 600°C and 900°C under matched sliding loads.
Changes in processing conditions, coating thickness, and substrate interactions may alter oxide composition, adhesion, and mechanical integrity.
Variation in oxide composition, adhesion, and mechanical integrity may influence wear resistance.
